sections.s03.s0: How a command-line tool behaves so that people and scripts can rely on it. Work items 1 to 4 in order on one small tool, rewriting it as you go; they cover most of what users notice. Items 5 to 9 are about configuration, output, installation and documentation, and each takes about an hour.
sections.s03.s1: A real CLI published to TestPyPI or PyPI. Write the subcommands and their tests first, add the --json output and exit-code tests, then package and install with pipx, and build the docs site last. Test the install on a clean machine or venv before calling it done.

s03.s0.0.how: Write a wordcount.py with argparse: one positional file argument, a --lines flag, and two subcommands via add_subparsers. Give every argument a help= string and read the output of -h for each subcommand.
s03.s0.0.done: Running the tool with -h and with each subcommand's -h prints accurate, complete help.

s03.s0.1.how: Rewrite the same tool with Typer using type hints, then with Click using decorators, and compare line counts and help output with the argparse version. Note what each framework adds: type conversion, testing helpers, completion.
s03.s0.1.done: You have the same interface in three versions and can say when a framework is worth the extra dependency.

s03.s0.2.how: Make the tool return 0 on success, 1 on a failed check and 2 on bad usage via sys.exit. Send errors and progress to sys.stderr and results only to stdout, then run tool args 2>/dev/null and check that stdout still holds only results.
s03.s0.2.done: Redirecting stderr leaves only machine-usable output, and echo $? shows the documented code in each case.

s03.s0.3.how: Accept - as a file name meaning stdin, and read with sys.stdin or fileinput when no file is given. Test it in a pipeline such as cat log.txt | tool count | sort, and handle a closed pipe by catching BrokenPipeError.
s03.s0.3.done: The tool works as a middle stage of a pipe and exits quietly when piped into head.

s03.s0.4.how: Load settings in this order, each overriding the last: built-in defaults, a TOML file read with tomllib, environment variables from os.environ, then command-line flags. Write a test that sets all four and checks the flag wins.
s03.s0.4.done: A test shows flags beat environment variables, which beat the file, which beats defaults; --help states the order.

s03.s0.5.how: Add a Rich Progress bar to a slow loop and print results as a Rich Table. Check Console.is_terminal, or sys.stdout.isatty(), and print plain lines when output is redirected to a file or pipe.
s03.s0.5.done: tool args > out.txt produces a file with no colour codes or progress-bar characters.

s03.s0.6.how: Add a [project.scripts] table to pyproject.toml pointing a command name at your main function, build with python -m build, and install the wheel with pipx install dist/*.whl. Run the command from a new terminal.
s03.s0.6.done: The command runs from any directory in a new shell, and pipx uninstall removes it cleanly.

s03.s0.7.how: Install completion for your Typer or Click tool with its --install-completion option or the documented shell snippet, and check that subcommands and options complete. Add a long description and usage examples to the top-level help.
s03.s0.7.done: Pressing Tab after the command name lists your subcommands in at least one shell.

s03.s0.8.how: Create a docs folder with mkdocs new, write a usage page for each subcommand, preview with mkdocs serve, then add a CI job that runs mkdocs gh-deploy or uploads the built site on each push to the main branch.
s03.s0.8.done: A push to the main branch updates the public docs site without any manual step.

s03.s1.0.how: Pick a task you currently do by hand in a terminal, list the subcommands it needs, and write the core functions with tests before adding the CLI layer. Keep argument parsing in one module and the work in another.
s03.s1.0.done: You use the tool yourself for the task, and each subcommand has at least one passing test.

s03.s1.1.how: Add a --json flag that builds a list or dict and prints it with json.dumps, with no other text on stdout. Pipe the output into python -m json.tool or jq to confirm it parses.
s03.s1.1.done: Every subcommand's --json output parses as valid JSON, checked by a test that calls json.loads on it.

s03.s1.2.how: Write a table of cases (success, failed check, bad arguments, missing file) with the expected exit code, and test each with Typer's or Click's CliRunner, or with subprocess.run and returncode.
s03.s1.2.done: Every documented exit code has a test that asserts it, and the suite passes.

s03.s1.3.how: Build an sdist and wheel with python -m build, upload to TestPyPI with twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*, then install with pipx on a clean machine or venv using the TestPyPI index.
s03.s1.3.done: A pipx install from the package index on a clean environment gives a working command.

s03.s1.4.how: Write mkdocs.yml and a docs folder in the repository with install, quick start and one page per subcommand. Build it in CI and deploy it with mkdocs gh-deploy or your host's build step.
s03.s1.4.done: The docs site is live, is rebuilt from the repository by CI, and every subcommand has a page.
